name: Gestao Hospital
description: The project aims to develop a Hospital Management System designed to organize and optimize resources within a public health system. The system addresses the challenge of managing a large and complex public health infrastructure, such as Brazil's Unified Health System (SUS), by providing a tool to prevent waste and maximize resource utilization, particularly in patient care.The system manages hospitals, each equipped with an inventory of various products, including a blood bank, and a specific number of beds. Its core functionalities include registering hospitals, recommending the closest hospital with available beds to a patient based on their location, and facilitating patient check-in and check-out processes. It also allows users to monitor available beds, register and manage product quantities in hospital stock, and oversee blood bank resources. A key feature is the ability to coordinate the transfer of necessary products, such as blood, from the nearest available hospital, while ensuring that each hospital retains a minimum stock for its own immediate needs.

transplante de órgãos, garantindo acesso integral, universal e gratuito para toda a população do país. Com a sua criação, o SUS proporcionou o acesso universal ao sistema público de saúde, sem discriminação. A atenção integral à saúde, e não somente aos cuidados assistenciais, passou a ser um direito de todos os brasileiros, desde a gestação e por toda a vida, com foco na saúde com qualidade de vida, visando a prevenção e a promoção da saúde. <div class="markdown-heading" dir="auto"><h2 tabindex="-1" class="heading-element" dir="auto">Objetivo</h2><a id="user-content-objetivo" class="anchor" aria-label="Permalink: Objetivo" href="#objetivo"><svg data-component="Octicon" class="octicon octicon-link" viewBox="0 0 16 16" version="1.1" width="16" height="16" aria-hidden="true"><path d="m7.775 3.275 1.25-1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1 4.95 4.95l-2.5 2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1-4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1 .018-1.042.751.751 0 0 1 1.042-.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l2.5-2.5a2.002 2.002 0 0 0-2.83-2.83l-1.25 1.25a.751.751 0 0 1-1.042-.018.751.751 0 0 1-.018-1.042Zm-4.69 9.64a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l1.25-1.25a.751.751 0 0 1 1.042.018.751.751 0 0 1 .018 1.042l-1.25 1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1-4.95-4.95l2.5-2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1 4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1-.018 1.042.751.751 0 0 1-1.042.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0-2.83 0l-2.5 2.5a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 0 2.83Z"></path></svg></a></div>
<p dir="auto">O objetivo do projeto é criar uma API para organizar um sistema público de saúde.</p>
<div class="markdown-heading" dir="auto"><h2 tabindex="-1" class="heading-element" dir="auto">Contextualização</h2><a id="user-content-contextualização" class="anchor" aria-label="Permalink: Contextualização" href="#contextualização"><svg data-component="Octicon" class="octicon octicon-link" viewBox="0 0 16 16" version="1.1" width="16" height="16" aria-hidden="true"><path d="m7.775 3.275 1.25-1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1 4.95 4.95l-2.5 2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1-4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1 .018-1.042.751.751 0 0 1 1.042-.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l2.5-2.5a2.002 2.002 0 0 0-2.83-2.83l-1.25 1.25a.751.751 0 0 1-1.042-.018.751.751 0 0 1-.018-1.042Zm-4.69 9.64a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l1.25-1.25a.751.751 0 0 1 1.042.018.751.751 0 0 1 .018 1.042l-1.25 1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1-4.95-4.95l2.5-2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1 4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1-.018 1.042.751.751 0 0 1-1.042.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0-2.83 0l-2.5 2.5a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 0 2.83Z"></path></svg></a></div>
<p dir="auto">O Sistema Único de Saúde (SUS) é um dos maiores e mais complexos sistemas de saúde pública do mundo, abrangendo desde o simples atendimento para avaliação da pressão arterial, por meio da Atenção Básica, até o transplante de órgãos, garantindo acesso integral, universal e gratuito para toda a população do país. Com a sua criação, o SUS proporcionou o acesso universal ao sistema público de saúde, sem discriminação. A atenção integral à saúde, e não somente aos cuidados assistenciais, passou a ser um direito de todos os brasileiros, desde a gestação e por toda a vida, com foco na saúde com qualidade de vida, visando a prevenção e a promoção da saúde. O objetivo desse projeto é criar uma ferramenta para auxiliar o SUS, evitar desperdício e potencializar os recursos a partir dos pacientes.</p>
<p dir="auto">Ao final do programa, além de apresentar a API criada, cada squad deverá expor quais são os pontos de melhoria e quais seriam os próximos passos no projeto, caso fossem seguir adiante.</p>
<div class="markdown-heading" dir="auto"><h2 tabindex="-1" class="heading-element" dir="auto">Requisitos técnicos obrigatórios</h2><a id="user-content-requisitos-técnicos-obrigatórios" class="anchor" aria-label="Permalink: Requisitos técnicos obrigatórios" href="#requisitos-técnicos-obrigatórios"><svg data-component="Octicon" class="octicon octicon-link" viewBox="0 0 16 16" version="1.1" width="16" height="16" aria-hidden="true"><path d="m7.775 3.275 1.25-1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1 4.95 4.95l-2.5 2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1-4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1 .018-1.042.751.751 0 0 1 1.042-.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l2.5-2.5a2.002 2.002 0 0 0-2.83-2.83l-1.25 1.25a.751.751 0 0 1-1.042-.018.751.751 0 0 1-.018-1.042Zm-4.69 9.64a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l1.25-1.25a.751.751 0 0 1 1.042.018.751.751 0 0 1 .018 1.042l-1.25 1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1-4.95-4.95l2.5-2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1 4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1-.018 1.042.751.751 0 0 1-1.042.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0-2.83 0l-2.5 2.5a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 0 2.83Z"></path></svg></a></div>
<p dir="auto">Para o projeto é necessário que as squads se utilizem dos aprendizados repassados pelo programa AceleraDev, portanto a solução deve ser construída de acordo com os seguintes requisitos:</p>
<ul dir="auto">
<li>Banco de dados;</li>
<li>Desenvolvimento do backend e APIs com Java Spring Boot;</li>
<li>Testes unitários são obrigatórios</li>
</ul>

<ul dir="auto">
<li>Todo hospital tem um estoque contendo diversos produtos.</li>
<li>Um estoque tem produtos e suas respectivas quantidades.</li>
<li>Dentro do estoque também tem banco de sangue</li>
<li>O hospital também possui leitos.</li>
<li>Ao encontrar um paciente é importante o recomendar para um hospital mais próximo e que tenha vaga disponível.</li>
<li>Caso o hospital precise de um produto, por exemplo, um banco de sangue, é importante fazer o envio do hospital mais próximo ao local.</li>
<li>Caso o hospital tenha apenas 4 itens ou 4 litros ele terá apenas o suficiente para o próprio hospital.</li>
</ul>

highLevelGoals: To quickly identify and be directed to the most suitable hospital with available beds based on their current location and needs.

To effectively monitor and manage the availability of hospital beds, ensuring efficient allocation for patient care.
To accurately track and manage the quantities of various products, including blood, within the hospital's stock.
To efficiently coordinate the transfer of necessary products, such as blood, from other hospitals while maintaining local minimum stock levels.
To oversee and optimize the utilization of all resources across the entire public health system to prevent waste and maximize efficiency.
To ensure that all hospitals maintain minimum required stock levels of essential products, especially blood, for immediate needs.
To coordinate and manage the strategic transfer of products between hospitals to meet system-wide demands and emergencies.
To gain a comprehensive overview of the health system's operational status, including bed availability and product inventories across all hospitals.

The Patient triggers the system to provide navigation instructions to the selected hospital.
The Patient confirms their pre-registered details upon arrival at the hospital to streamline the admission process.

The Hospital Staff modifies the total bed capacity for a specific ward within their hospital.
The Hospital Staff adjusts the count of currently occupied beds for a specific ward.
The Hospital Staff retrieves and displays the current bed availability status for all wards in their hospital.
The Hospital Staff updates the status of a specific bed to 'occupied' upon a patient's admission.
The Hospital Staff updates the status of a specific bed to 'available' after a patient's discharge.
The Hospital Staff registers a new type of product (e.g., blood type, medication) into the hospital's inventory system.
The Hospital Staff modifies the current quantity of a specific product in the hospital's inventory.
The Hospital Staff logs the consumption of a specific quantity of a product from the inventory.
The Hospital Staff retrieves and displays the current stock levels for all products in their hospital's inventory.
The Hospital Staff defines the minimum acceptable quantity for a specific product in their hospital's inventory.
The Hospital Staff initiates a request to another hospital for a specific product transfer.
The Hospital Staff reviews and approves a product transfer request received from another hospital.
The Hospital Staff reviews and rejects a product transfer request received from another hospital.
The Hospital Staff checks the current status of product transfer requests they have initiated to other hospitals.
The Hospital Staff retrieves a list of product transfer requests from other hospitals awaiting their review and action.
The Health System Administrator retrieves aggregated data on bed availability across all hospitals in the public health system.
The Health System Administrator retrieves aggregated data on product inventory levels across all hospitals in the public health system.
The Health System Administrator queries the system to find hospitals that have an excess of specific resources.
The Health System Administrator queries the system to find hospitals that are experiencing a shortage of specific resources.
The Health System Administrator defines the minimum required stock levels for critical products across all hospitals in the system.
The Health System Administrator queries the system to pinpoint hospitals whose stock of a critical product has fallen below the defined minimum level.
The Health System Administrator configures the system to receive automated notifications when a hospital's critical product stock falls below the minimum threshold.
The Health System Administrator commands the system to arrange a strategic transfer of products between specified hospitals.
The Health System Administrator reviews and approves a product transfer request that was initiated by a hospital.
The Health System Administrator retrieves a comprehensive record of all past and current system-wide product transfers.
The Health System Administrator temporarily bypasses a hospital's local minimum stock level to facilitate an urgent product transfer.
The Health System Administrator accesses a real-time visual dashboard displaying bed occupancy rates across all hospitals.
The Health System Administrator generates a report detailing the stock levels of critical products across all hospitals.
The Health System Administrator retrieves historical data to analyze trends in resource utilization over specified periods.
The Health System Administrator requests the generation of a report to aid in strategic capacity planning for a specific region or the entire system.

baselineCritiques.actors: The identified actors are generally appropriate for the described system. "Patient" covers the end-users receiving care, "Hospital Staff" covers the operational management of beds and inventory, and "Health System Administrator" covers the high-level coordination and oversight of the public health infrastructure. However, the description explicitly mentions "recommending the closest hospital... based on their location." This implies an interaction where a user (potentially a patient, a relative, or a triage operator) queries the system for recommendations. While "Patient" is listed, it is often ambiguous whether patients directly interact with the system or if it is done by staff. Given the "Hospital Staff" role is broad, it likely covers the operational side. The main potential omission is a specific "Triage Officer" or "Dispatcher" if the recommendation feature is distinct from general staff duties, but "Hospital Staff" is a reasonable abstraction. The set is complete enough to represent the core interactions without significant contradiction.
baselineCritiques.highLevelGoals: The high-level goals are well-aligned with the software description and actors. They correctly capture the core functionalities: patient routing based on location and bed availability, check-in/check-out processes, inventory management (including blood banks), and inter-hospital resource coordination with minimum stock constraints. The goals are functional, strategic, and appropriately attributed to the respective actors. There are no contradictions or significant omissions regarding the described system capabilities.
baselineCritiques.lowLevelGoals: The low-level goals are well-structured, functional, and align closely with the high-level goals and the software description. They correctly decompose the strategic objectives into specific user actions (e.g., "Mark Bed as Occupied", "Request Product Transfer"). The coverage is comprehensive, addressing patient care, staff resource management, and administrator oversight. There are no obvious contradictions or major omissions regarding the core functionalities described (hospital registration, bed management, inventory, blood bank, and inter-hospital transfers). The distinction between actors is maintained appropriately.

hlg_749536d82f97fe7c_001.reconstructed_high_level_goal: The Patient identifies a suitable hospital by providing geographical coordinates and medical conditions, retrieves a filtered list of nearby hospitals with available beds, views detailed information for a selected hospital, and obtains navigation instructions to reach it.
hlg_749536d82f97fe7c_001.rationale: This High-Level Goal comprehensively describes the Patient's process of finding and navigating to a hospital. llg_001 contributes the capability for the Patient to provide their current geographical coordinates to enable location-based hospital search. llg_002 adds the capability for the Patient to select or input their specific medical condition or required specialty to filter hospital recommendations. llg_003 provides the capability for the Patient to send a query and retrieve a list of nearby hospitals with available beds matching their specified medical needs. llg_004 includes the capability for the Patient to select a recommended hospital and view its detailed information, such as address, contact, and specific services. llg_005 completes the goal by adding the capability for the Patient to trigger the system to provide navigation instructions to the selected hospital.

hlg_2eb718edc8460b1b_001.reconstructed_high_level_goal: The Patient confirms their pre-registered details upon arrival at the hospital for admission, and accesses personalized discharge instructions and follow-up care plans, and acknowledges their successful discharge from the hospital via the system.
hlg_2eb718edc8460b1b_001.rationale: This high-level goal integrates all distinct capabilities from the low-level goals. llg_001 contributes the capability for the Patient to confirm pre-registered details upon arrival for admission. llg_002 adds the capability for the Patient to access personalized discharge instructions and follow-up care plans. llg_003 provides the capability for the Patient to acknowledge their successful discharge from the hospital. The reconstructed goal explicitly includes both the admission and discharge/follow-up phases, reflecting all distinct functional aspects.

hlg_b3685f96076f153a_001.reconstructed_high_level_goal: The Hospital Staff inputs and saves new hospital details, and manages bed resources by modifying total ward bed capacity, adjusting occupied bed counts for specific wards, updating specific bed statuses to 'occupied' upon patient admission or 'available' after patient discharge, and retrieving and displaying current bed availability status for all wards.
hlg_b3685f96076f153a_001.rationale: llg_001 contributes the capability for the Hospital Staff to input and save details of a new hospital. llg_002 adds the capability for the Hospital Staff to modify the total bed capacity for a specific ward. llg_003 adds the capability for the Hospital Staff to adjust the count of currently occupied beds for a specific ward. llg_004 adds the capability for the Hospital Staff to retrieve and display the current bed availability status for all wards in their hospital. llg_005 adds the capability for the Hospital Staff to update the status of a specific bed to 'occupied' upon a patient's admission. llg_006 adds the capability for the Hospital Staff to update the status of a specific bed to 'available' after a patient's discharge.

hlg_d030e7a187e5a8e2_001.reconstructed_high_level_goal: The Hospital Staff manages the hospital's product inventory by registering new product types, modifying current product quantities, logging product consumption, defining minimum acceptable product quantities, and retrieving and displaying current stock levels for all products.
hlg_d030e7a187e5a8e2_001.rationale: The reconstructed high-level goal encompasses all distinct functional capabilities present in the low-level goals. llg_001 contributes the capability for Hospital Staff to register new types of products into the inventory system. llg_002 adds the ability for Hospital Staff to modify the current quantity of a specific product. llg_003 includes the functionality for Hospital Staff to log the consumption of products from the inventory. llg_004 provides the capability for Hospital Staff to retrieve and display current stock levels for all products. llg_005 introduces the ability for Hospital Staff to define minimum acceptable quantities for specific products in the inventory.

replacement_request.generation_project_description:
The project aims to develop a Hospital Management System designed to organize and optimize resources within a public health system. The system addresses the challenge of managing a large and complex public health infrastructure, such as Brazil's Unified Health System (SUS), by providing a tool to prevent waste and maximize resource utilization, particularly in patient care.The system manages hospitals, each equipped with an inventory of various products, including a blood bank, and a specific number of beds. Its core functionalities include registering hospitals, recommending the closest hospital with available beds to a patient based on their location, and facilitating patient check-in and check-out processes. It also allows users to monitor available beds, register and manage product quantities in hospital stock, and oversee blood bank resources. A key feature is the ability to coordinate the transfer of necessary products, such as blood, from the nearest available hospital, while ensuring that each hospital retains a minimum stock for its own immediate needs.

Rewrite the functional intention for actor 'Hospital Staff' using this focus: Expand the goal to include 'Register Hospital' alongside bed monitoring and management, ensuring the description covers both the creation of hospital records and the management of bed availability.

The original HLG 'Monitor System Performance and Capacity' is supported by the documentation, which explicitly states the system allows users to 'monitor available beds' and 'register and manage product quantities'. The HLG outcomes are {view bed availability, view product inventories}. The reconstruction HLG' outcomes are {access bed occupancy dashboards, generate critical stock reports, retrieve historical trends, request capacity planning reports}. HLG' entails the core monitoring capabilities of the HLG (beds and stock). However, HLG' adds 'historical trends' and 'capacity planning reports', which are specific analytical outputs not explicitly enumerated in the original HLG's concise description of 'operational status'. While these are likely valid LLGs, the reconstruction is broader than the parent's stated scope. The parent is a valid, supported high-level goal. The divergence suggests the LLGs may be over-specified or the parent description is slightly narrow, but the parent itself is not materially wrong or unsupported. It is distinct from siblings like 'Ensure System-Wide Resource Optimization' (which focuses on optimization actions/identification of surplus/deficit) and 'Guarantee Critical Stock Availability' (which focuses on setting levels/alerts). Therefore, the parent is kept, and the LLGs require evaluation to ensure they align with the 'monitoring' scope or if the parent needs minor clarification (though KEEP is preferred for valid parents with partial overlap in reconstruction). Voting result 3/3 for REGENERATE_LOW_LEVEL_GOALS. The decomposition is not supported by the documentation. The project description explicitly states the system allows users to 'monitor available beds' and 'register and manage product quantities', but it does not mention 'real-time visual dashboards', 'historical data', 'trends', or 'strategic capacity planning reports'. These are invented features (llg_001, llg_003, llg_004) that go beyond the documented scope of monitoring current status. While llg_002 aligns with monitoring stock levels, the specific framing as a 'report' is a minor implementation detail, but the other three LLGs introduce unsupported capabilities. The parent goal 'Monitor System Performance and Capacity' is satisfied by checking current bed availability and stock levels, not by generating historical trend analyses or strategic planning reports which are not documented.

hlg_dc1f0b2826ae0958_001.rationale: Voting result 2/3 for REWRITE_ORIGINAL_HIGH_LEVEL_GOAL. The original HLG is a generic umbrella ('Optimize Hospital Resource Management and Setup') that conflates multiple distinct documented responsibilities: hospital registration, bed management, inventory control, blood bank management, and internal transfers. The documentation supports these as separate functional areas (e.g., 'registering hospitals', 'monitoring available beds', 'register and manage product quantities', 'oversee blood bank resources', 'coordinate the transfer'). The reconstruction HLG' accurately aggregates the LLGs but inherits the same over-broad scope. Crucially, sibling branches 'Maintain Accurate Inventory Control' and 'Facilitate Inter-Hospital Resource Coordination' already cover specific subsets of this umbrella. The original HLG is not a single recognizable actor-owned functional outcome but a collection of independent outcomes. It is materially malformed due to lack of precise functional boundaries. It should be rewritten to focus on a specific, recoverable intention, such as 'Manage Hospital Bed Availability' or 'Register and Maintain Hospital Records', as the current scope is too broad to be a valid HLG.

replacement_request.generation_project_description:
The project aims to develop a Hospital Management System designed to organize and optimize resources within a public health system. The system addresses the challenge of managing a large and complex public health infrastructure, such as Brazil's Unified Health System (SUS), by providing a tool to prevent waste and maximize resource utilization, particularly in patient care.The system manages hospitals, each equipped with an inventory of various products, including a blood bank, and a specific number of beds. Its core functionalities include registering hospitals, recommending the closest hospital with available beds to a patient based on their location, and facilitating patient check-in and check-out processes. It also allows users to monitor available beds, register and manage product quantities in hospital stock, and oversee blood bank resources. A key feature is the ability to coordinate the transfer of necessary products, such as blood, from the nearest available hospital, while ensuring that each hospital retains a minimum stock for its own immediate needs.

Rewrite the functional intention for actor 'Hospital Staff' using this focus: Narrow the scope to a single distinct documented outcome, such as 'Manage Hospital Bed Availability' (covering ward capacity, occupancy, and bed status) or 'Register and Maintain Hospital Records' (covering hospital details). Exclude inventory, blood bank, and transfer capabilities which are covered by other HLGs or should be separate HLGs.

hlg_1228e2cbab58c0da_001.rationale: Voting result 2/3 for KEEP_ORIGINAL_HIGH_LEVEL_GOAL. The original HLG expresses the intent to 'coordinate and manage the strategic transfer of products'. The reconstructed HLG' aggregates four distinct outcomes: (1) commanding transfers, (2) approving requests, (3) viewing history, and (4) overriding minimum stock. The original HLG's description ('coordinate and manage... transfer') semantically entails the first two outcomes (initiation and approval are core coordination tasks) and arguably the fourth (overriding stock is a management action to facilitate transfer). However, the original HLG does not explicitly entail 'viewing system transfer history' (llg_003), which is a monitoring/audit function rather than a direct coordination action. While 'manage' is broad, in requirements engineering, 'coordinate transfer' typically refers to the active execution/approval workflow, not the passive retrieval of historical logs. Therefore, HLG' adds an outcome (history retrieval) not strictly entailed by the original HLG's specific phrasing, making the relationship PARTIAL_OVERLAP. The original HLG is supported by the documentation ('coordinate the transfer of necessary products'). The parent is valid but the reconstruction is broader. Thus, the parent should be kept, and the LLGs need evaluation to determine if 'View System Transfer History' is a valid child or if the parent needs slight expansion to explicitly include monitoring/auditing of transfers. Furthermore, llg_002 (Approve Hospital-Initiated Transfer Request) is unsupported; the documentation assigns the coordination of transfers to the Health System Administrator and mentions Hospital Staff coordinating from other hospitals, but does not document a formal request-approval workflow initiated by hospitals for the Administrator to review. llg_003 (View History) is also not explicitly documented as a distinct capability for the Administrator, who is described as overseeing optimization and ensuring stock levels, not necessarily maintaining a historical audit log of transfers. hlg_749536d82f97fe7c_001.rationale: Voting result 3/3 for KEEP_ORIGINAL_HIGH_LEVEL_GOAL. The original HLG 'Access Timely Hospital Care' expresses the outcome of identifying and being directed to a suitable hospital. The material outcome set is {identify suitable hospital, be directed to it}. The reconstruction HLG' expresses {provide coordinates, specify needs, retrieve list, view details, obtain navigation}. HLG' entails HLG because retrieving a list and obtaining navigation constitutes being directed. However, HLG does not explicitly entail the specific sub-steps of 'viewing details' or 'specifying medical needs' as distinct functional boundaries, though they are implied by 'identify'. More critically, the documentation states the system 'recommends the closest hospital... based on their location'. It does not explicitly support 'medical needs' or 'specialty' filtering, nor does it explicitly support 'navigation instructions' (only 'directed to'). The LLGs introduce 'medical needs' and 'navigation' which are not explicitly in the project description. The parent HLG is valid as it captures the core documented outcome of location-based recommendation. The reconstruction adds unsupported details (medical needs, navigation) and is therefore not equivalent. The parent is supported, so it should be kept, but the LLGs need evaluation to remove unsupported features. Voting result 3/3 for KEEP_LOW_LEVEL_GOALS. The decomposition accurately reflects the parent goal 'Access Timely Hospital Care'. llg_001 supports 'based on their current location' by capturing coordinates. llg_002 supports 'based on... needs' by capturing medical conditions. llg_003 supports 'identify... hospital with available beds' by retrieving the filtered list. llg_004 supports 'identify... most suitable' by allowing the patient to view details to make an informed selection. llg_005 supports 'be directed to' by providing navigation instructions. All LLGs are explicitly grounded in the project description's core functionality of recommending the closest hospital with available beds based on location and needs. No essential capabilities are missing, and no LLGs are unsupported or redundant.

hlg_2eb718edc8460b1b_001.rationale: Voting result 3/3 for KEEP_ORIGINAL_HIGH_LEVEL_GOAL. The original HLG 'Experience Seamless Admission and Discharge' expresses the material outcome set {check-in, check-out} for the Patient. The documentation explicitly supports 'facilitating patient check-in and check-out processes'. The reconstructed HLG' expresses the set {confirm pre-registration, access discharge instructions, acknowledge discharge}. While 'confirm pre-registration' entails the check-in phase and 'acknowledge discharge' entails the check-out phase, the reconstruction adds 'access discharge instructions' which is not explicitly stated in the original HLG's description ('checking into and out of'). Conversely, the original HLG's broad 'seamless/streamlined' scope is not fully captured by the specific LLG actions, but the core functional outcomes (admission and discharge) are present in both. However, the reconstruction is a lossless aggregate of the LLGs, which are specific steps within the admission/discharge process. The original HLG is a valid, supported parent goal. The relationship is PARTIAL_OVERLAP because the reconstruction details specific sub-tasks (like retrieving instructions) that are not explicitly enumerated in the high-level description, though they are implied by the process. The parent is valid and supported by the documentation. Therefore, the original HLG should be kept, and the LLGs need evaluation to ensure they correctly decompose the 'seamless' aspect or if the HLG description needs to be more precise to match the LLGs. Given the strict equivalence requirement, since HLG' adds 'access instructions' which is not in HLG's text, it is not EQUIVALENT. It is PARTIAL_OVERLAP. The parent is valid. Voting result 3/3 for REGENERATE_LOW_LEVEL_GOALS. The decomposition is incomplete and contains unsupported details. The project description explicitly states the system facilitates 'patient check-in and check-out processes'. The current LLGs omit the core 'Check-in' (admission) and 'Check-out' (discharge) actions, replacing them with 'Confirm pre-registration' and 'Acknowledge discharge'. 'Confirming pre-registration' is not explicitly documented as a distinct patient capability; the documentation only mentions 'check-in'. Similarly, 'acknowledging' discharge is a specific UI interaction not entailed by the general 'check-out' process. Furthermore, 'Retrieve Discharge Instructions' and 'follow-up care plans' are not mentioned in the project description, which focuses on resource management, bed availability, and inventory. These LLGs introduce undocumented functionality and fail to capture the essential check-in/check-out capabilities required by the parent HLG.

hlg_50bc4605094e00ea_001.rationale: Voting result 3/3 for KEEP_ORIGINAL_HIGH_LEVEL_GOAL. The original HLG 'Guarantee Critical Stock Availability' expresses the outcome of ensuring hospitals maintain minimum stock levels. The documentation supports this by stating the system ensures 'each hospital retains a minimum stock for its own immediate needs' and the actor 'ensures... minimum stock levels'. The reconstructed HLG' 'Enable... to define and update minimum required stock levels' captures the specific mechanism (defining/updating levels) but omits the broader outcome of 'ensuring' or 'guaranteeing' the availability itself, which implies monitoring or enforcement beyond just setting the parameters. However, the single LLG 'Set System-Wide Minimum Stock Levels' only covers the configuration aspect. The original HLG is a valid, supported stakeholder outcome. The reconstruction is a partial overlap because it focuses on the configuration action rather than the full guarantee outcome, or potentially the LLGs are incomplete. Since the parent is valid and supported, but the reconstruction/LLGs may not fully capture the 'guarantee' aspect (which might involve monitoring or alerts not present in the single LLG), we keep the parent and require LLG evaluation to ensure the decomposition covers the full scope of 'guaranteeing' availability, not just setting the threshold. hlg_1228e2cbab58c0da_001.reconstructed_high_level_goal: The Health System Administrator can manage product transfers across the health system by initiating transfers of specified products and quantities between hospitals, retrieving and viewing historical transfer logs, querying current product stock levels across all hospitals to identify transfer sources, viewing aggregated current product demand across all hospitals to prioritize strategic transfers, and viewing configured minimum product stock levels at individual hospitals to monitor compliance and inform transfer decisions.
hlg_1228e2cbab58c0da_001.rationale: The reconstructed high-level goal losslessly aggregates all distinct functional capabilities from the provided low-level goals. llg_001 contributes the core capability to initiate a transfer of a specified product and quantity from a selected source hospital to a designated destination hospital. llg_002 adds the ability to retrieve and view a historical log of all product transfers that have occurred across the health system. llg_003 provides the functionality to query the system to identify the current stock levels of a specific product in all hospitals within the network to determine potential source hospitals for transfers. llg_004 introduces the capability to view aggregated current demand for specific products across all hospitals in the health system to prioritize strategic transfers. Lastly, llg_005 contributes the ability to view the configured minimum stock levels for specific products at individual hospitals to monitor compliance and inform transfer decisions. Each low-level goal describes a unique aspect of managing and informing product transfers within the health system, and all are explicitly included in the high-level goal without generalization or omission.

hlg_29a3f737d15593b7_001.reconstructed_high_level_goal: Enable the Health System Administrator to retrieve system-wide consolidated dashboards and reports providing real-time bed availability and occupancy rates, and detailing current inventory levels for critical medical products across all hospitals, highlighting items below minimum stock thresholds.
hlg_29a3f737d15593b7_001.rationale: llg_001 contributes the capability for the Health System Administrator to retrieve a consolidated dashboard displaying real-time bed availability and occupancy rates across all hospitals in the health system. llg_002 contributes the capability for the Health System Administrator to retrieve a report detailing current inventory levels for critical medical products across all hospitals, highlighting items below minimum stock thresholds. The reconstructed goal integrates these distinct information retrieval capabilities, covering both operational capacity (beds) and critical resource management (medical products) for the Health System Administrator across the entire health system.

hlg_1228e2cbab58c0da_001.rationale: Voting result 3/3 for KEEP_ORIGINAL_HIGH_LEVEL_GOAL. The original HLG 'Enable Strategic Resource Allocation' is supported by the documentation, which explicitly mentions coordinating the transfer of products between hospitals. The material outcome set of the HLG is {coordinate, manage, transfer}. The reconstructed HLG' aggregates the LLGs into {initiate transfer, view history, query availability, view demand, view minimum stock}. HLG' entails the core 'transfer' outcome but adds specific monitoring and informational capabilities (history, demand, stock levels) that are not explicitly stated in the original HLG's description, which focuses on the coordination and management of the transfer itself. While the LLGs support the reconstruction, the original HLG is a valid, high-level abstraction of the transfer coordination process. The relationship is PARTIAL_OVERLAP because HLG' is more specific and includes auxiliary monitoring tasks not explicitly in the HLG text, though they are part of the 'manage' scope. The parent is valid and supported, so it should be kept, and the LLGs need evaluation to ensure they align with the 'strategic' aspect. Voting result 3/3 for REGENERATE_LOW_LEVEL_GOALS. The decomposition is incomplete and contains unsupported capabilities. llg_002 (View System Transfer History) and llg_004 (View Current Product Demand) are not explicitly stated or necessarily entailed by the project description, which focuses on coordinating transfers based on stock availability and minimum levels, not on historical logs or aggregated demand metrics. Furthermore, the parent HLG 'Enable Strategic Resource Allocation' explicitly includes managing transfers to 'meet system-wide demands and emergencies' while ensuring 'minimum stock' retention. The current LLGs lack the essential capability to validate or enforce that a transfer does not deplete the source hospital below its configured minimum stock level, which is a core constraint mentioned in the description ('ensuring that each hospital retains a minimum stock'). While llg_005 allows viewing these levels, it does not cover the enforcement or validation logic required for the strategic allocation goal. Therefore, the LLGs must be regenerated to remove unsupported features and add the missing minimum stock validation capability.

hlg_29a3f737d15593b7_001.rationale: Voting result 3/3 for REMOVE_ORIGINAL_HIGH_LEVEL_GOAL. The original HLG 'Monitor System Performance and Capacity' is supported by the documentation, which explicitly allows users to 'monitor available beds' and 'register and manage product quantities'. The original branch is a redundant fragment of the broader sibling goal.

replacement_request.generation_project_description:
The project aims to develop a Hospital Management System designed to organize and optimize resources within a public health system. The system addresses the challenge of managing a large and complex public health infrastructure, such as Brazil's Unified Health System (SUS), by providing a tool to prevent waste and maximize resource utilization, particularly in patient care.The system manages hospitals, each equipped with an inventory of various products, including a blood bank, and a specific number of beds. Its core functionalities include registering hospitals, recommending the closest hospital with available beds to a patient based on their location, and facilitating patient check-in and check-out processes. It also allows users to monitor available beds, register and manage product quantities in hospital stock, and oversee blood bank resources. A key feature is the ability to coordinate the transfer of necessary products, such as blood, from the nearest available hospital, while ensuring that each hospital retains a minimum stock for its own immediate needs.

Rewrite the functional intention for actor 'Health System Administrator' using this focus: Expand the goal to include retrieving detailed bed occupancy dashboards and generating reports for critical stock levels, in addition to aggregated availability and surplus/deficit identification.

This goal also encompasses the ability to identify hospitals with resource surpluses or deficits and generate critical stock reports to proactively manage resource distribution, prevent waste, and ensure minimum stock levels are maintained throughout the public health system.

actor.name: Health System Administrator
actor.description: Oversees the entire public health system, coordinates inter-hospital resource transfers, and ensures optimal resource utilization and minimum stock levels across the network.

low_level_goals.name: Retrieve System Critical Stock Report
low_level_goals.description: Allow the Health System Administrator to generate a report detailing critical stock levels for products and blood banks across the public health system, highlighting items below minimum thresholds.

hlg_749536d82f97fe7c_001.reconstructed_high_level_goal: The Patient identifies a suitable hospital by providing geographical coordinates and medical conditions, retrieves a filtered list of nearby hospitals with available beds, views detailed information for a selected hospital, and obtains navigation instructions to reach it.
hlg_749536d82f97fe7c_001.rationale: This High-Level Goal comprehensively describes the Patient's process of finding and navigating to a hospital. llg_001 contributes the capability for the Patient to provide their current geographical coordinates to enable location-based hospital search. llg_002 adds the capability for the Patient to select or input their specific medical condition or required specialty to filter hospital recommendations. llg_003 provides the capability for the Patient to send a query and retrieve a list of nearby hospitals with available beds matching their specified medical needs. llg_004 includes the capability for the Patient to select a recommended hospital and view its detailed information, such as address, contact, and specific services. llg_005 completes the goal by adding the capability for the Patient to trigger the system to provide navigation instructions to the selected hospital.

hlg_2eb718edc8460b1b_001.reconstructed_high_level_goal: The patient provides identification details, enters personal and medical history details, reads and confirms understanding of admission terms and conditions, and verifies the accuracy of submitted admission information for hospital admission; and for hospital discharge, signals readiness to begin the procedure, reviews and confirms the accuracy of personal and medical information, reads and confirms understanding of discharge terms and conditions, and verifies the accuracy of discharge information.
hlg_2eb718edc8460b1b_001.rationale: The reconstructed high-level goal encompasses all distinct capabilities from the low-level goals. llg_001 adds the capability for the patient to provide identification details to initiate the hospital admission process. llg_002 adds the capability for the patient to enter personal and relevant medical history details for hospital admission. llg_003 adds the capability for the patient to read and confirm understanding of the hospital's admission terms and conditions. llg_004 adds the capability for the patient to verify the accuracy of their submitted admission information before finalization. llg_005 adds the capability for the patient to signal their readiness to begin the hospital discharge procedure. llg_006 adds the capability for the patient to review and confirm the accuracy of their personal and medical information relevant to the discharge process. llg_007 adds the capability for the patient to read and confirm understanding of the hospital's discharge terms and conditions. llg_008 adds the capability for the patient to verify the accuracy of their discharge information before finalization. The goal explicitly includes both hospital admission and discharge processes, reflecting the distinct but related phases covered by the LLGs, without generalizing or discarding any specific action or information type.

hlg_1228e2cbab58c0da_001.rationale: The reconstructed high-level goal losslessly aggregates all distinct functional capabilities from the provided low-level goals. llg_001 contributes the core capability to initiate a transfer of a specified product and quantity from a selected source hospital to a designated destination hospital. llg_002 adds the ability to retrieve and view a historical log of all product transfers that have occurred across the health system. llg_003 provides the functionality to query the system to identify the current stock levels of a specific product in all hospitals within the network to determine potential source hospitals for transfers. llg_004 introduces the capability to view aggregated current demand for specific products across all hospitals in the health system to prioritize strategic transfers. Each low-level goal describes a unique aspect of managing and informing product transfers within the health system, and all are explicitly included in the high-level goal without generalization or omission.

hlg_93ae286ddf03ddb7_001.rationale: Voting result 3/3 for KEEP_ORIGINAL_HIGH_LEVEL_GOAL. The original HLG 'Manage Hospital Bed Availability' is supported by the documentation, which explicitly mentions 'monitor available beds' and 'patient check-in and check-out processes' (implying status updates). The material outcome set of the HLG is {monitor, update status}. The reconstructed HLG' aggregates the LLGs into {configure capacity, adjust counts, manage individual status, retrieve overviews, retrieve specific status}. HLG' entails the HLG's outcomes (monitoring is covered by retrieval; updating is covered by status changes). However, HLG' includes specific operational details (configuring max capacity, adjusting ward counts) that are not explicitly enumerated in the HLG's concise description, making the relationship PARTIAL_OVERLAP rather than strict EQUIVALENT. The parent is valid and not redundant with siblings (Inventory or Transfers). Therefore, the parent is kept, and the LLGs require evaluation to ensure they align with the documented scope. Voting result 2/3 for REGENERATE_LOW_LEVEL_GOALS. The decomposition is incomplete. The parent HLG explicitly aims to ensure accurate information for 'patient admissions, transfers, and discharges'. While llg_004 and llg_005 cover the status changes for admission (occupied) and discharge (available), there is no LLG covering the status change required for 'transfers' (e.g., marking a bed as 'transferred' or handling the specific state change when a patient moves to another bed/ward without a full discharge). Furthermore, llg_006 and llg_007 introduce 'out of service' and 'in service' states. While maintenance is a real-world scenario, the project description and parent HLG focus on patient care flow (admission/discharge/transfer) and resource optimization, not facility maintenance scheduling. The documentation does not explicitly entail 'out of service' as a distinct stakeholder goal separate from 'available' in the context of patient flow; it is an inferred operational detail not grounded in the provided text's core functionalities (registering, recommending, check-in/out, monitoring). More critically, the lack of a specific LLG for the 'transfer' aspect of bed status management (distinct from simple available/occupied toggles which might imply discharge/admission) creates a gap in the 'transfers' requirement. However, looking closer at the prompt's strictness: 'transfers' in the context of bed availability usually implies the bed becomes available for the next patient or the patient moves. If 'transfer' means moving a patient to another bed, the source bed becomes available (llg_005) and the destination becomes occupied (llg_004). Thus, the core states are covered. The main issue is llg_006 and llg_007. The documentation mentions 'monitor available beds' and 'check-in/check-out'. It does not mention maintenance or 'out of service' status. These are unsupported additions. Therefore, regeneration is required to remove the unsupported maintenance states.

hlg_93ae286ddf03ddb7_001.rationale: This high-level goal is a lossless reconstruction that incorporates every distinct functional capability from the low-level goals. llg_001 contributes the capability to update the total number of beds available in a specific ward. llg_002 adds the capability to update the count of occupied beds within a specific ward. llg_003 provides the capability to view an overview of bed availability across the hospital or specific wards. llg_004 introduces the capability to change the status of a specific bed to 'occupied' for patient admissions or transfers. llg_005 adds the capability to change the status of a specific bed to 'available' after a patient discharge or transfer. Finally, llg_006 contributes the capability to retrieve the current status of an individual bed by its identifier. All distinct actions (update, change status, view, retrieve) and objects (total beds, occupied beds, individual bed status, bed availability overview) are explicitly preserved.
